Mechanism: Front / profile / three-quarter turnaround plus a costume plate, generated once per character and frozen
Where it lives / tool: CharacterAnchors.csv plus examples/doubao_character_sheet_prompt.md as the template
What it guarantees: A single physical reference every later shot is compared against
Breaks when: The sheet itself is regenerated or re-styled mid-project
Binding strength: Reference only, not enforceable on its own
Verification: Side-by-side of any shot against the sheet
Common failure: Redrawing the sheet per episode so nothing is actually locked
Fix action: Freeze one sheet per character version and never regenerate it

Mechanism: Anchor sentences stored verbatim and copied byte-identical into every prompt. No synonym substitution
What it guarantees: That the identity description cannot drift between episodes
Breaks when: Someone paraphrases the sentence to fit a scene
Binding strength: P0 enforceable by string diff against the registry
Verification: Diff the prompt string against the registry row
Common failure: 泪痣 rewritten as 斑点 or 小痣 on a later episode
Fix action: Restore the registry text verbatim and regenerate
Evidence: Structural rule P0 enforceable by string diff

Mechanism: Map each reference slot to one role: subject / costume / style / environment. Never re-describe a referenced face
What it guarantees: Identity carried by the image rather than by adjectives
Breaks when: Two slots given conflicting roles, or the face re-described in text
Binding strength: Strong inside one model family, not portable
Verification: Slot count and role per slot recorded in the iteration log
Common failure: Face drifts because the prompt re-describes it after attaching a reference
Fix action: Delete the face description from the prompt and keep the slot binding

Mechanism: Use the character sheet frame or the previous shot's last frame as the image-to-video input
What it guarantees: Continuity across the cut rather than across the episode
Breaks when: The first frame itself already drifted
Verification: First frame compared against the sheet
Common failure: Chaining drift: each shot is fine but shot 60 no longer looks like L0
Fix action: Fall back to the sheet frame instead of the previous shot

Mechanism: Freeze seed plus the parameter block for a given shot family
What it guarantees: Reproducibility: the same input yields the same identity
Breaks when: The model version changes under the frozen seed
Verification: Recorded seed replays to the same result
Common failure: Assuming a stored seed survives a model version bump
Fix action: Re-lock the seed after any model update and log the version

Mechanism: Train a per-character LoRA from the sheet set
What it guarantees: Highest identity fidelity across long series
Breaks when: Too few training images, or a style clash with the target model
Verification: Holdout frames generated from unseen prompts
Common failure: Training on fewer than roughly 15-20 images, which overfits the poses you trained on
Fix action: Add coverage (angles, expressions, lighting) before retraining
Evidence: [评估: 训练集规模经验值, 验证方式=留出集盲测相似度]

Mechanism: The first shot of every episode regenerates from the L0 sheet and its last frame is re-checked before the episode proceeds
What it guarantees: That drift is caught at the start of an episode rather than at shot 60
Breaks when: The episode is assembled out of order so the first shot lands last
Verification: First-shot frame compared against the sheet before any other shot is generated
Common failure: Building the episode backwards and only discovering drift at the end
Fix action: Regenerate the opening shot from L0 before continuing

Mechanism: Always run L0 through L3. Add L4 always. Add L5 only when the series exceeds roughly 30 shots per character, because below that the training cost exceeds the regeneration cost
Where it lives / tool: Params.csv style decision recorded in ChangeLog row
What it guarantees: A predictable cost curve instead of stacking every layer by default
Breaks when: Adding L5 at project start for a 10-shot pilot
Binding strength: Not a fidelity guarantee - a cost rule
Verification: Compare regeneration count against training cost per character
Common failure: Training a LoRA before knowing the character survives the pilot script
Fix action: Defer L5 until the shot count justifies it
